articles.headline: Commanders QB Daniels will play, WR Diggs out against Giants
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will start Sunday in his return from an elbow injury but wide receiver Stefon Diggs will not play against the Giants due to a hamstring injury.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダーズのQBダニエルズは出場、WRディグスはジャイアンツ戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダーズのクォーターバック、ジェイデン・ダニエルズは肘の怪我から復帰し日曜日に先発出場するが、ワイドレシーバーのスティーフォン・ディグスはハムストリングの怪我のためジャイアンツ戦を欠場する。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will start Sunday, but he will be minus one of his top receivers.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn said receiver Stefon Diggs won't play because of a hamstring injury suffered in a Week 4 loss to the Colts. But Quinn said receiver Terry McLaurin "looked really good" in practice Friday but stopped short of saying he would definitely play.

The Commanders (1-3) host the Giants (3-1) Sunday in a key divisional game. Washington already is 0-2 in the NFC East.

Washington also will return right guard Sam Cosmi, who missed two games with a concussion and running back Rachaad White, who missed last season with a shoulder injury.

McLaurin did not play vs. the Colts because after injuring his hamstring two days before the game. McLaurin is third on the Commanders with 10 receptions and second with 141 yards.

Diggs did not participate in practice all week, though he did go through stretching Thursday before heading to a separate field for work with the team's athletic trainers. But he was not on the field Friday during the portion open to the media.

Diggs leads Washington with 18 catches for 170 yards and three touchdowns.

Daniels' return from a dislocated left elbow had been expected all week. He was limited in practice when the team worked in London, but the goal was to make sure he was ready vs. the Giants. Daniels will play with a brace on his non-throwing elbow for the rest of the season. The brace keeps his elbow slightly bent.

Daniels said he can do everything necessary with the brace on, such as handoff and take snaps from center.

Daniels was a full participant all week and offensive coordinator David Blough said Thursday that there would be no limitations with the game plan because of his elbow.

"He's full go," Blough said.

Daniels has finished only five games since the start of the 2025 season. He dislocated his elbow in Week 10 last year and returned in Week 14 only to re-aggravate the injury after getting shoved to the ground and landing on his left arm.

Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis will backup Daniels. Washington could opt to sign Sam Hartman to the active roster off the practice squad and make him the emergency third quarterback.

articles.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Stroud, Washington among top options
articles.description: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール直前の補強候補：ストラウドやワシントンらが有力な選択肢に
articles.descriptionJa: 怪我やバイウィーク、厳しい対戦カードなどでラインナップの調整が必要な方に向けて、マット・ボーエンが潜在的な候補をリストアップします。
articles.body:
At various points during the fantasy football season, injuries, bye weeks and breaking news can cause you to need reinforcements for your fantasy lineup. Every Friday throughout the 2026 NFL season, Matt Bowen will offer some late-week pickup options at each of the primary fantasy positions to help fill those holes, with an emphasis on deeper leagues.

Because of that, this column will focus mostly on players rostered in fewer than 50% of ESPN leagues, with occasional exceptions.

The Week 5 NFL schedule features some really tough matchups for fantasy football, starting with the quarterback position. However, I still have four options -- in the QB2 range -- who have some upside. There are also a handful of wide receivers below, including deeper-league fliers you can take a chance on. As always, we'll hit on the running back and tight ends, and I have two available defenses to stream this week.

Quarterbacks

 Kirk Cousins, Las Vegas Raiders (33.3% rostered; at Patriots)

Cousins has scored 20 or more points in three straight games, and he has thrown two or more touchdown passes in all four games this season. Now, Cousins isn't going to provide any upside as a runner. We know that. But in Klint Kubiak's offense, one that leans on tight end usage, Cousins can play on rhythm. And the Raiders are going to throw the ball in scoring position, as Cousins' eight red zone touchdown passes are tied for second most in the league. He's a superflex starter in the road matchup versus the Patriots.

 C.J. Stroud, Houston Texans (41.1% rostered; at Titans)

Stroud benefited from the return of wide receiver Nico Collins in Week 4, producing a season-high 23.08 points in a prime matchup versus Dallas. Collins had 118 yards receiving, plus he scored two touchdowns on end zone throws. It's a much tougher matchup this week versus the Titans, but Stroud is scoring 17.1 PPG, and Collins is the difference-maker in the Houston route tree. Stroud has value here as a QB2 in superflex formats.

 Jordan Love, Green Bay Packers (48.9% rostered; vs. Bears)

Love averages 16.2 fantasy PPG and has thrown two touchdown passes in all four games played. And due to a subpar rushing attack in Green Bay, Love is attempting 38.5 passes per game. Yes, the Bears defense ranks in the top 12 versus quarterbacks, but I do see positive perimeter matchups here for Packers wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. If you need a QB2 this week, Love does have some value.

 Deshaun Watson, Cleveland Browns (15.7% rostered; at Jets)

Watson (16.7 fantasy PPG) has scored 19 or more points in two of four games played, and he's averaging 31.8 rushing yards per game. The Jets defense ranks in the top five versus quarterbacks, so I don't love the matchup. However, if you need a QB2 with dual-threat upside Watson fits. articles.headline: Fantasy football: Why now is the ideal time to trade Derrick Henry
articles.description: The ageless back is off to a strong start, which presents the opportunity to maximize the return in a deal.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール：なぜ今がデリック・ヘンリーをトレードする絶好のタイミングなのか
articles.descriptionJa: 年齢を感じさせないこのRBは好スタートを切っており、トレードによるリターンを最大化する好機となっている。
articles.body:
Derrick Henry has continued to go toe to toe with Father Time like no running back in recent history. He is once again off to a hot start, scoring 22.7 fantasy points per game, fourth among RBs entering Week 5. Only Jahmyr Gibbs, Kenneth Walker III and Bijan Robinson have scored more fantasy points at the position. That is despite Henry being 10th at the position in yards from scrimmage (seven touchdowns in four games helps). Perhaps he'll score 30 TDs like he is on pace for, but it would not be wise to count on that.

Reasons for concern on Henry

When you dive into the numbers, there are worrisome signs. Looking at his stats since 2020, he is posting personal lows in a number of metrics, including yards per carry (tied), yards after contact per carry and max speed. In addition, his explosive run rate is the lowest it has been since he joined the Ravens. His forced missed tackles rate is the second lowest in this span, just ahead of last season. That is concerning because last season his rate was higher in the first month, and we saw it decline as the season went on.

One thing that has worked in Henry's favor is his 2.0 yards before contact (his highest in this sample), partly because he has faced loaded boxes at the lowest rate since 2021. Things have broken right for the King during the first month of the season. With QB Lamar Jackson injured now, you can expect teams to put their defensive focus on Henry and stack the box against him.

Henry has been known to finish strong, so I looked at only his first four weeks in this sample as well to see how it stacks up. He is below average in yards per carry, forced missed tackles rate, yards after contact -- which is by far his lowest in this sample -- explosive run rate, as well as average and max speed.

Typically, you would not overreact, as Henry has been plenty productive. However, with him set to turn 33 years old in less than three months, the declining metrics are concerning, especially because he is unlikely to keep scoring touchdowns at this rate. That means he is going to need his yardage totals to increase to remain at this fantasy pace.

Another issue is that he is not often used in the passing game. He has only seven targets on the season. That hurts his value in PPR leagues, as a running back target (on average) is worth 2.5 times as much as a carry.

It would not be a bad idea to make Henry available in your league and see what you could get in return. Could Henry be fine and continue to produce at an RB1 level? Certainly. But if you can move him for another top back or receiver, you mitigate any risk of a late-season/career drop-off.

Which players should you target in a trade for Henry?

Some RBs I would move him for are Jonathan Taylor, Christian McCaffrey, James Cook III, Ashton Jeanty, Chase Brown and Kyren Williams, all of whom have fewer fantasy points than Henry at the moment. The top fantasy receivers are also an option.

articles.headline: Knicks tabling Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart contract talks
articles.description: The Knicks have said they are tabling contract extension talks with Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart "until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."
articles.headlineJa: ニックス、カール＝アンソニー・タウンズとジョシュ・ハートとの契約交渉を延期
articles.descriptionJa: ニックスは、カール＝アンソニー・タウンズおよびジョシュ・ハートとの契約延長交渉を「シーズン後半まで」延期し、現在は開幕への準備にのみ専念すると発表した。
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are tabling all contract extension talks with key players Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart, the franchise announced Friday.

"As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of," a team spokesperson said in a statement to ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday. "As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Towns is eligible for a four-year deal worth over $276 million. He is due $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for next season.

The Knicks' latest offer to Towns was a four-year deal worth approximately $200 million, sources told Charania.

Towns has been vocal about his frustrations with the now-tabled talks.

"Simply put, I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday. "None of those things have come close to happening."

A six-time All-Star, Towns was a catalyst for the Knicks' playoff run last season, averaging 15.9 points, 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists as New York won the title in a five-game Finals over the San Antonio Spurs.

Hart is eligible for a contract extension as well, he will make $20.9 million this season and there's a team option for $22.3 million in 2027-28.

"There hasn't really been much movement and conversation with that, so I don't think it will get done," Hart said on media day last month. "I would love to get it done."

Additionally, Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby will be eligible for contract extensions next offseason.

After the Knicks ended their 53-year title drought, owner James Dolan said the team will not go into the second spending apron, which means tough decisions will need to be made. New York did not re-sign backup center Mitchell Robinson this offseason. Robinson, who was the longest-tenured Knick on last year's team, signed with the Boston Celtics.

New York has the second-best odds at DraftKings to win this year's title and become the first team to repeat as champion since the 2016-17 and 2017-18 Golden State Warriors.

Information from ESPN's Vincent Goodwill was used in this report.

articles.headline: Xabi Alonso insists Cole Palmer committed to representing England after Thomas Tuchel dig
articles.description: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to representing England following question marks raised by national team boss Thomas Tuchel.
articles.headlineJa: シャビ・アロンソ、トーマス・トゥヘルの皮肉に対し、コール・パーマーのイングランド代表への意欲を強調
articles.descriptionJa: チェルシーのアロンソ監督は、代表監督のトーマス・トゥヘルが疑問を投げかけたことについて、コール・パーマーがイングランド代表としてプレーすることに意欲的であると主張した。
articles.body:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to representing England following question marks raised by national team boss Thomas Tuchel.

Tuchel said Blues forward Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play international football after he withdrew from his country's squad ahead of Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

The 24-year-old has since trained with his club and been declared fit for Saturday's Premier League clash with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso also expects Reece James, Moisés Caicedo and João Pedro to be available as the Blues bid to bounce back from a thumping 3-0 loss at Brentford three weeks ago.

"He has trained the last week, he has felt better," Alonso said of Palmer, who pulled out of England duty due to reported load management.

"We didn't want to rush because we've had enough time.

"The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, he's feeling OK.

"In the Brentford game, we could see he was struggling. For the next part, we have good feeling with him and that he's feeling better.

"He's committed [to England] but he has to be fully fit to play. And when he's fully fit he will enjoy his minutes. We need him in that moment: the club and the national team."

- Man City 'a disgrace; I would throw them out' - furious Ian Holloway

- Was epic Man City-Liverpool rivalry all a sham after cheating scandal?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

Palmer was left out of Tuchel's World Cup squad and has featured just three times since the German took charge of England in January 2025.

Blues captain James missed the recent international window amid another hamstring issue, while striker Pedro sat out the Brentford defeat because of a knee injury, and midfielder Caicedo has played only 14 minutes all season due to a persistent calf problem.

"Yes, he's ready to go," Alonso said of Caicedo.

"We have used the time with Moi to be back fit. He's been training good and he's OK to go."

Asked about James, Palmer and Pedro, the Spaniard continued: "They have been able to train, some of them earlier than others.

"We have used the time, and that was the plan. We knew that against Brentford we were with some players struggling but now they have trained well and they are ready to go.

"For the next block of games until the next international break, we have five Premier League games and hopefully they will be available as long but for tomorrow they will be good."

Former Bayer Leverkusen and Real Madrid boss Alonso began his reign with back-to-back league wins but has taken just one point from the last nine available.

"It's going to take time," he said. "We need to keep improving, keep learning. From each game we are learning things but we need to ensure we don't make the same mistakes again, knowing that each game is really tough."

articles.headline: Dejan Kulusevski, Pedro Porro to travel with Tottenham squad for Man United clash despite injuries
articles.description: Dejan Kulusevski will travel with Tottenham to Manchester United on Saturday but he is only set to offer support along with injured defender Pedro Porro.
articles.body:
Dejan Kulusevski will travel with Tottenham to Manchester United on Saturday but he is only set to offer support along with injured defender Pedro Porro.

Swedish attacker Kulusevski has not played competitively for more than 500 days after multiple setbacks following a serious patella injury in his right knee at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

There is finally light at the end of the tunnel for Kulusevski, who stepped up his recovery during the international break after he played in an 11-v-11 match against Spurs' academy, and boss Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged a long-awaited return is close.

"He is working well, tomorrow he comes with us, also Porro [for support]. I want all players tomorrow, tonight and tomorrow," De Zerbi said.

"I think he is an example for everyone, Dejan Kulusevski. Forget the player, but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed this time, was an example, a reference for everyone."

Quizzed on when he might play, De Zerbi admitted: "I don't know, it's not just my responsibility. We are working together with the medical staff. They are working very well with him, they have done special work. We have to analyse week by week."

De Zerbi will have James Maddison available at Manchester United, but the playmaker has encountered more fitness struggles over the past week.

Maddison has also not started for Tottenham in 17 months after back-to-back knee injuries and had to sit out a number of training sessions before the trip to Old Trafford.

- Tottenham's Xavi Simons enrolls at Harvard Business School

- Premier League reranked: Have we found Arsenal's fatal flaw?

"He is available but he lost three to four days in the beginning of this week and the end of the last week," De Zerbi said.

"He is a good guy, he suffered to stay not on the pitch, to have the injury. Now it was not a big injury. Tomorrow he can play, but the Premier League is tough.

"Physically it is a very strong competition and you have to be in the right physical condition to compete, to run, to fight. He is a No. 10, a different player, but I think he is working well and this is the way.

"The way is to complete three, four, five weeks in a row without problems, without feeling pain, without feeling problems. And then he is a normal player, he has nothing special, bad."

De Zerbi confirmed Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke are both available despite fitness problems with the Netherlands.

The Italian also acknowledged he has been waiting for this United fixture since Spurs' 3-2 loss to Aston Villa on Sept. 19.

"I've been waiting for this game for three weeks," De Zerbi said. "I wanted to play the day after [Villa]."

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye McTominay as Napoli talks stall
articles.description: Scott McTominay's contract talks at Napoli have hit a hurdle, with Real Madrid reportedly interested in making a move. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Scott McTominay's contract talks at Napoli have stalled, with Real Madrid reportedly interested in making a move. Plus, Chelsea are keeping an eye on Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid have contacted Scott McTominay's representatives amid stalled contract talks with Napoli, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Scotland midfielder could also attract approaches from Premier League clubs if an agreement remains elusive. Napoli may nevertheless block a January departure, keeping their star player for the remainder of the season while allowing themselves more time to negotiate an extension. As a result, any potential transfer is likely to be pushed back until next summer.

- Chelsea are monitoring Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong's situation ahead of the January transfer window, reports Spanish outlet Sport. Barça will assess the 29-year-old's playing time as he returns from a knee injury, with increased midfield competition potentially limiting his opportunities. Chelsea remain attentive after sanctioning Enzo Fernández's move to Manchester City, while Barcelona have not ruled out any scenario. However, De Jong remains determined to stay and reclaim a starring role under Hansi Flick.

- Bayern Munich are monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion center back Luka Vuskovic, German journalist Christian Falk reports. The Croatia international is interested in joining Bayern, but the German champions would first need to offload Kim Min-Jae or Hiroki Ito to create space and funds for another defender. Vušković, who impressed on loan at Hamburg last season, remains on their shortlist, although Bayern are unable to make an offer as it stands.

- Real Madrid forward Endrick is open to joining AC Milan on loan in January, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. The 20-year-old has indicated that Milan would be among his preferred destinations if Madrid sanctions a winter departure, having struggled for playing time this season. AS Roma and Aston Villa are also interested, but Milan could benefit from owner Gerry Cardinale's strong relationship with Endrick's representatives at Roc Nation. Any move remains dependent on Madrid's approval.

- Real Madrid expect Michael Olise to sign a new contract with Bayern, Sky Germany reports. Bayern have held preliminary talks over a contract extension as his current deal runs until 2029, with improved terms potentially making him the club's highest-paid player. A move to Madrid remains a possibility, but Olise is likely to stay if the Spanish giants do not make a concrete approach. Bayern may consider letting him leave the club if renewal talks fail.
